name: Tanner's Creek Blended Bourbon
description: Tanner's Creek Blended Bourbon is distilled by MGP Ingredients in Lawrenceburg, Indiana and, as their motto goes, is "Made by Hoosiers for Hoosiers." This Indiana exclusive whiskey is made from a blend of high-rye bourbons as well as other whiskeys all made at the Indiana distillery. Tanner’s Creek is named for a waterway that has been used to transport grain, barrels and whiskey. Bottled at 85 proof.

name: 15 Stars Platinum Bourbon
description: 15 Stars Platinum Bourbon is a blend of straight bourbons sourced from "America's First West." These bourbons were aged 10, 15, and 18 years and hailed from Kentucky, Indiana, and Tennessee. Additionally, these bourbons were made with differing mash bill recipes. Available beginning July 19, 2023 in KY, IN, TN, MO, GA, and LA. (SRP $279.99)

name: Barrell Bourbon 10th Anniversary Blend
description: Released in September 2023 to celebrate the brand's 10th anniversary, this bottling includes some of BCS's most noteworthy batches (011 & 021). This anniversary blend contains straight bourbons from Tennessee (8, 13, 17, & 18 years-old), Indiana (8 & 9 years-old), and Kentucky (8 year-old). It is an extremely limited release with availability online and in person at the Kentucky Bourbon Festival. Additional availability begins September 18, 2023 at the brand's blending & bottling facility in Jeffersontown, KY. (SRP $84.99)

name: Wilderness Trail Bottled in Bond Single Barrel Bourbon (Wheated Bourbon)
description: Wilderness Trail Bottled in Bond Single Barrel Bourbon is made with a mash bill of 64% corn, 24% wheat, 12% malted barley. The corn and wheat are grown by a local farm and the grain bill uses a sweet mash rather than a sour mash like many bourbons use. Bottled without chill-filtration at 100 proof. Each bottle lists barrel number. As with all single barrel releases, expect variations in taste.

name: Door County Rye Whiskey
description: Door County Distillery Rye comes from Shipwrecked Brew Pub, a microbrewery in Egg Harbor, WI. This rye is distilled using the naturally limestone filtered water of Door County, WI. It is bottled at 40% ABV.

name: Daddy Rack Single Barrel Cask Strength Tennessee Whiskey
Company Distilling Tennessee Whiskey Finished with Apple Wood
caskType: new, charred American oak, finished with apple wood
description: Company Distilling Tennessee Whiskey Finished with Apple Wood is produced by under the direction of Founder and Master Distiller Jeff Arnett, formerly of Jack Daniel's. The whiskey is mellowed through sugar maple charcoal using the Lincoln County Process and matured in charred American oak barrels before undergoing a finishing period with toasted apple wood. Bottled at 86.5 proof, the proof point references the 865 area code of East Tennessee where the distillery is based.

name: Roaming Man Tennessee Straight Rye Whiskey Batch 10
Leiper's Fork Single Barrel Cask Strength Tennessee Whiskey
description: Leiper's Fork is a grain-to-glass distillery located in Williamson County, Tennessee. This is made with a mash bill recipe of 70% corn, 15% rye, and 15% malted barley. Unlike most of the core whiskeys in the brand's portfolio, this is not a bottled in bond expression. This bottling is sold as a single barrel expression and is bottled at cask strength so expect variances in the both the flavor and proof from barrel to barrel. It is charcoal filtered post-distillation prior to barrel aging.

name: Jack Daniel's Heroes Selection  Single Barrel Tennessee Whiskey
Nashville Barrel Company Single Barrrel Tennessee Whiskey Cask Strength - Barrel # 1461
Jack Daniel's Tennessee Whiskey 'A-Team' Private Barrel Selection (2023)
Tommy Rotter CIDER CASK FINISHED TENNESSEE STRAIGHT WHISKEY
Jack Daniel's Single Barrel Heritage Barrel Tennessee Whiskey (2018 Special Release)
caskType: toasted, then charred new American oak barrels
description: Announced in fall 2018, Jack Daniel's Single Barrel Heritage Barrel is a limited edition release for the brand's single barrel series. As is the case for all Jack Daniel's whiskeys, the barrels were constructed at the brand's own cooperage facility. Master distiller Jeff Arnett selected 200 American white oak barrels to be toasted and then charred. Additionally, the whiskey entered the barrel at 100 proof, a lower proof than is typically used for Jack Daniel's. The whiskey matured at the top of the highest elevated warehouses on Coy Hill. Bottled at 100 proof, this is a US exclusive release.

name: 1792 Full Proof Straight Bourbon
description: 1792 Full Proof Bourbon is a release from Barton 1792. The warehouses in which the bourbon was stored are exposed to direct sunlight through 7 story-high windows, with metal frames and concrete bottom floors. The aged distillate was filtered once though a plate and frame filter (no chill filtering) in order to maintain its proof. It's bottled at the same proof at which it entered the barrel — 125 proof.

tastingNotes.full: Scents of honey, bananas, pears and golden apple waft from the glass along with some faint phenol notes. These sweet and fruity aromas are repeated on the palate with a taste similar to Honey Nut Cheerios cereal sprinkled with cinnamon and clove. Some lemon oil tartness and slight bitterness come out in the finish. This bourbon definitely needs a big ice cube to smooth out the flavors and soften the alcoholic heat.

name: Barrell Bourbon Batch 029
description: Barrell Spirits Batch 029 Bourbon consists of a combination of bourbons taken from 6, 7, 9, 10, 14 and 16 year old barrels that were distilled in Kentucky, Tennessee and Indiana. They were exclusively aged in new American white oak, and bottled at 115.88 proof. This bottling is available as of June, 2021.

tastingNotes.full: The nose is somewhat tight and quiet, but things open up considerably on the palate. Flavors of dark chocolate, hot spices (both peppery and sweet, such as clove) and a slightly medicinal note are bound by a dominant salty, tart and tangy quality. A large rock would likely quiet that tartness and bring out more of the sweetness and spice. Often the word "interesting" as a negative connotation when it comes to spirits tasting, but here it should be taken in its literal meaning: this whiskey is interesting! In a good way!

name: Burnside Bourbon
description: Burnside Bourbon is a 4 year-old bourbon bottled at 96 proof by Eastside Distilling in Portland, Oregon.

tastingNotes.full: With notes of cotton candy and caramel, the aroma of Burnside bourbon suggests a whiskey on the sweeter side. This is confirmed upon sipping; despite a bit of heat from its relatively high proof, this a fairly sweet bourbon. Experienced drinkers may look for a little more complexity, but it makes for an approachable entry to the category.

name: Old Forester 100 Proof Bourbon
description: Old Forester 100 Proof Bourbon is part of Brown-Forman’s historic lineup, a brand first introduced in 1870 as one of the first bourbons sold exclusively in sealed bottles. The name is often linked to a doctor who prescribed whiskey for medicinal purposes, though the signature on each bottle belongs to founder George Garvin Brown. It is bottled at 100 proof and is also available in an 86 proof version.

tastingNotes.full: The initial nose boasts a powerful whiff of alcohol that fades to yeasty bread. Given a little time to breathe, the scent of crème brûlée, brown sugar, and woody floor wax make themselves known. Taste starts off with minty bitterness and chocolate, like an Andes Mint made with dark chocolate. Vanilla and oak appear shortly thereafter, followed by dryness, wood, and fire from the high proof. The finish is warm and lingers, giving off a rye spiciness, though not particularly long. This is a business bourbon with little in the way of subtlety but an excellent reflection of Brown-Forman's urban setting.

name: Four Roses Small Batch Select Bourbon
description: This is a non-chill filtered bourbon using a recipe selected by Master Distiller Brent Elliott. Four Roses has 10 bourbon recipes available to craft its bourbon offerings which are made from two different mash bills and five different yeast strains. Small Batch Select is made from six of the ten: OBSV, OBSK, OBSF, OESV, OESK, OESF. Each bourbon in the small batch selection will be six or seven years old. This is the first new brand extension for the brand in 12 years. It joins the other permanent releases for the brand. Availability begins spring 2019 in Kentucky, Texas, California, New York, and Georgia with other locations to follow in the future. (SRP $59.99)

tastingNotes.full: Cocoa powder dusted dark chocolate truffles shine through on the nose, with spearmint gum, spicy oak, and earthy-leather undertones. The palate offers salted caramel and peanut shells, along with licorice, oak, and baking spices, with a bit of a sharp astringency coming through towards the back. This one stays chocolate through and through, with chocolate syrup, Peppermint Patties, and barrel char closing the show.

name: 1792 Single Barrel Bourbon
description: 1792 Single Barrel Bourbon is the third limited edition bottling released by the brand. Select barrels of this high-rye straight Kentucky bourbon are chosen from the brand's Bardstown, Kentucky rickhouses.

tastingNotes.full: An unexpected breeze of pineapple, pear, banana, and tart lemon greet the nose and palate. With further sips, rich vanilla, toffee and butterscotch enrich the fruitiness. The spice comes in at the end in the form of black pepper, clove, allspice, and cinnamon. All together, the whiskey is nicely balanced with a flash of drying heat that travels down the throat.

name: Elijah Craig Barrel Proof Bourbon (Batch Releases)
description: Released for the first time in the March 2013, each batch is a an uncut, unfiltered selection of Elijah Craig 12 Year. Each batch will vary both in flavor and in proof as is the nature of such releases. The "code" for the batches is as follows: The first letter of each batch indicates the order of the release for that year beginning with the letter "A" for the first batch, "B" for the second, and so on. Next is a number which reflects the month of the release, so "1" for January for example. The third and fourth digits reflect the year of the release. This batch number is printed on the front of each bottle along with the proof.

tastingNotes.full: The nose will knock you off your feet. Lots of rye, barrel, heath bar and leather. The palate is ridiculously viscous, with cinnamon candies, rye, barrel, roasted vanilla bean and chocolate. The finish is long, smooth and robust with spice, roasted chestnuts and barrel.

name: Weller Full Proof Bourbon
description: Weller Full Proof Bourbon is a wheated bourbon distilled at the Buffalo Trace Distillery. Bottled at 114 proof, this is the same proof as when the spirit entered the barrel for maturation. The Kentucky straight bourbon is bottled without chill filtration. This is a limited release that will be released annually. The first offering is June 2019.

tastingNotes.full: Baked apples and vanilla are showcased on the nose, along with fiery cinnamon. The palate offers vanilla bean, baking spices, sour cherries, and cassia bark. The finish turns to the drier and more medicinal side, with spearmint, tannic oak, leather, and milk chocolate truffles. Quite sippable despite the high proof, with a pleasantly lengthy finish.

name: Copper Pony Rye Whiskey
description: This expression is a small batch rye. It is bottled at 45% ABV.

name: (ri)1 Straight Rye Whiskey
description: The unique named whiskey, pronounced "Rye One", is a rye whiskey from Beam Global. Released in the fall of 2008, it is comprised of a blend of rye whiskeys, with the youngest being 4 1/2 years of age. It is bottled at a respectable 92 proof and has quite the eye-catching stark label.

tastingNotes.full: The spice notes are quite pronounced on the nose and in fact are a bit prickly. Once you jump that hurdle, you'll discover a sticky sweet and vanilla'd underlining. The rye is on the thin side and bitter and dry with a bit of leather on the palate. As you exhale, you'll find lots of char smoke and red apple skins. This is a decent rye, but there are older (and better) whiskeys on the market sold for much less.

name: Coppercraft Rye Whiskey
description: This expression is a rye whiskey that is blended from a house-distilled rye age a minimum 2 years and sourced rye from other distilleries. It is bottled at 90 proof.

name: High Plains Rye Whiskey
description: This is a rye whiskey blended by Jim Rutledge from a combination of American ryes from Kentucky Artisan Distillery (Kentucky), Middle West Distillery (Ohio), MGP (Indiana), and NY Distilling Co. (Brooklyn, NY). Each rye is at least 4 years old with varying mash bills between 51% up to 100% rye. It is bottled at 48.5% ABV.

name: Doc Brewer's Rye Whiskey
description: Blackfish Spirits Distillery in Auburn, Washington distills from locally grown grain. Their Brewer's Rye is made from malted rye and barley.

tastingNotes.full: Young rye whiskeys have a tendency to be all spice and no subtlety. Thankfully, despite pouring with a pale straw hue, Doc Brewer's malted rye breaks that mold. It's much softer on the palate and its time in barrel doesn't obscure the grain, which comes through with a very pleasant cereal quality, light floral notes, and just the right amount of heat. It's not too brash and vanilla just floats in the background; a very nice, light whiskey overall.

name: Davidson Reserve Tennessee Straight Bourbon Whiskey Single Barrel
Jack Daniel's Single Barrel Heritage Barrel Tennessee Whiskey (2019 Special Release)
caskType: toasted then charred new American oak
description: This 2019 release of Jack Daniel's Single Barrel Heritage Barrel is the second batch of this limited edition series for the Tennessee whiskey brand which first launched in 2018. This 2019 release is a year older than the previous version. As is the case for all Jack Daniel's whiskeys, the barrels were constructed at the brand's own cooperage facility. Master distiller Jeff Arnett and his team selected fewer than 200 American white oak barrels to be toasted and then charred. Bottled at 100 proof, this is a US exclusive release available as of October 2019.

Treaty Oak Experimental Collection Cask Strength Tennessee Whiskey 16 Years (16th Anniversary Release)
Wild Turkey Rare Breed Barrel Proof Bourbon
description: Wild Turkey Rare Breed is made with a blend of 6, 8, and 12 year-old Kentucky straight bourbon whiskeys. This is bottled at barrel proof so each batch will vary slightly in proof from batch to batch.

tastingNotes.full: The nose offers spice and spearmint, with vanilla sweetness hiding behind heat. The palate opens with brown sugar and vanilla, leading into burnt toast and char. Sultry smooth all the way through even with its hefty proof. Dry oak and spice come out on the finish with pine, mint, and the lingering rich sweetness of vanilla in myriad forms, think: vanilla frosting, pudding, and pound cake. (review from spring 2017 batch. 116.8 proof)

name: Fistful of Bourbon
description: Released by William Grant & Sons, Fistful of Bourbon is made by blending five straight bourbons sourced from one or more undisclosed sources. The blended American whiskey uses no neutral grain in its composition. Bottled at 90 proof, it is set for September 2018 release with Texas seeing it first before it rolls out to other markets nationally.

tastingNotes.full: Red Hots and ginger snaps star on the nose, along with vanilla taffy and spearmint. The palate starts with a hit of tannic oak and cedar wood, as well as baking spices and menthol. Then vanilla comes on and shares its space with the oak and spice. Fiery cinnamon stays at the forefront through the medium length finish, with more vanilla and mint.

name: DIGITS Bourbon
description: DIGITS Bourbon is made in collaboration with Dave Phinney, Napa Valley winemaker and owner of Savage & Cooke Distillery, and former NBA champion and Hall of Famer Scottie Pippen. DIGITS, named for Pippen's large hands, is sourced bourbon from Tennessee and Indiana aged up to 5 years. It finishes aging on Mare Island where Savage & Cooke is located and then bottled at 92 proof.

name: Penelope Bourbon
description: This is the flagship bourbon for the brand which is named after the founder's daughter, Penelope. The bourbon is made from a blend of three different mash bill recipes from the same producer (MGP in Indiana). Four different grains are used in those mash bills: corn, wheat, rye, and malted barley. The bourbon is aged for 2-3 years in new, charred American oak barrels, but there's a twist here. The barrel heads are charred to #2 level(medium char) and the staves are #4 (heavily charred). It's bottled in batches at 80 proof without chill filtration.

name: Breuckelen 77 Straight Bourbon Whiskey Single Barrel (The Prime Bourbon & Breaking Bourbon)
Four Roses Yellow Label Bourbon
description: Four Roses Yellow Label is a Kentucky straight bourbon and is the entry-level bourbon for the brand. Four Roses has two separate mash bills they can use for their bourbons. One is labeled recipe "B" and is 60% corn, 35% rye, and 5% malted barley. The other is recipe "E" and is 75% corn, 20% rye, and 5% malted barley. Both mash bills are utilized for this bottling. Additionally, Four Roses uses up to five different yeast strains for their bourbons. All are used here. Over time, the Yellow Label bottle has changed with the label losing the yellow color. Beginning in spring 2018, the name for this product is simply "Four Roses Bourbon".

description: Borough Bourbon is brought to you by the female-owned distillery, Republic Restoratives in Washington, D.C. Released in November 2016, the distillery sourced this straight bourbon whiskey from Bardstown, Kentucky and  finished it in French oak barriques previously used in the production of Sauvignon Blanc. It is bottled at 44% ABV.

name: Widow Jane The Vaults 15 Year Bourbon (2021 Release)
description: This is the 2021 release of the limited edition library series from Widow Jane. It consists of 15 and 17 year old straight bourbons that have been selected by Widow Jane president and head distiller Lisa Wicker from the brand’s Conover Street rickhouse in Red Hook, Brooklyn. It is bottled at 49.5% ABV with 3,000 bottles available as of December, 2021.

tastingNotes.full: The nose is sweet and potent, with vanilla bean, treacle, and salted caramel, along with spearmint and cinnamon. The palate is rich, with dark fudge in front of tannic oak, cloves, and black pepper. The finish is lengthy, luscious, and dripping with maple and chocolate syrups, along with closing notes of cedar wood, peanut shells, and barrel char.

name: Wilderness Trail Bottled in Bond Small Batch Bourbon (High Rye Bourbon)
description: This expression uses a rye-forward mash bill rather than wheat as the secondary grain, composed of 64% corn, 24% rye, and 12% malted barley. The corn and rye are sourced from a local farm, and the whiskey is produced using a sweet mash process instead of the more common sour mash method. Each small batch is blended from 10–12 barrels and bottled in bond at 100 proof without chill-filtration. It debuted in April 2019 as the third whiskey release from the Danville, Kentucky–based distillery.

tastingNotes.full: The nose is a pleasing swirl of spring herb notes of thyme and mint mixing with red apples and cinnamon. The palate exhibits flavors of roasted peanuts and caramel along with sharper spices of clove, black pepper, and hot cinnamon. The whiskey has a dense weight that coats the tongue, but with measured sweetness. The finish lingers with underlying earthiness and spice.

name: 10th Mountain Rye Whiskey
description: This distillery gets its name from the original 10th Mountain soldiers from the 1940s. Located in Vail, Colorado, 10th Mountain's spirits are infused with the mountain lifestyle. This whiskey is produced using a 65% rye mash bill and aged for two winters in new oak barrels.

tastingNotes.full: Deep gold in color the whiskey has strong rye spice and oak in the bouquet. Sweet notes of caramel and butterscotch are found with a full-bodied, spicy umami mid-palate. The rye has a lingering spicy finish with notes of chocolate and nutmeg.

Watershed Bourbon
caskType: new, charred American oak, apple brandy barrels
description: This bourbon is one of the first whiskeys to debut in the distillery's reimagined whiskey portfolio for 2021. It is a tri-blend made by blending Watershed's standard bourbon with its six-year apple brandy finished bourbon, and a sourced bourbon selected specifically for its flavor profile. It is a 4 year age statement offering bottled at 90 proof, available as of June, 2021.

tastingNotes.full: The whiskey has a refreshing nose of apples growing in a pine forest. The palate is slightly medicinal, with some breakfast cereal toastiness and caramel corn sweetness. Tart plum and baked apple come into the mid palate with very subtle baking spices. This isn't one of those big, whalloping bourbons, but it has its own character.

name: Bardstown Bourbon Co. Goose Island Bourbon County Stout Finish
caskType: finished in Goose Island Bourbon County Stout barrels
description: This whiskey from BBCo. was made in collaboration with Chicago-based Goose Island Brewery. Beginning with a blend of 6 & 7 year-old Kentucky straight bourbon, the blend was further aged in freshly-dumped Goose Island Bourbon County Stout barrels. Then BBCo. added 9 year-old Kentucky  straight bourbon to finish the blend. There are approximately 3,500 9L cases available of this Collaborative Series release. It's bottled at a cask strength of 100 proof and is available online and nationwide at select retailers beginning September 2023. (SRP $159.99)

tastingNotes.full: The stout finish isn't super noticeable on the nose, but you get pleasant cherry and freshly cut apples along with bright vanilla and milk chocolate. The bourbon has a moderate heft to it and a lightly slick body. There's a bittersweet taste with a moderate barrel spiced profile. Additionally, you'll find a beery/yeasty taste on the edges. Upon exhaling, the coffee/chocolate stout notes appear and almost a savory/meaty note. Maybe serve it with a steak to intensify those notes. Overall, a pleasant bourbon.

name: Bardstown Bourbon Company Single Barrel New Braunfels Bourbon Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey Barrel Strength
Stellum Single Barrel Bourbon Cask Strength Straight Bourbon Whiskey SB Vega G3 (Seduction In A Bourbon Bottle)
Backbeat Bourbon
description: 3 Howls Distillery got their name from the legend of Cù-Sìth. This giant hound would take souls into the underworld by howling 3 times. This selection was distilled in copper pot stills and bottled at 46% ABV.

name: Fortuna Bourbon
description: Fortuna is a Kentucky bourbon brand which was originally founded in the late 1800s and last bottled in the 1950s. The brand has since been revived by the folks behind the Rare Character Whiskey, a purveyor of American whiskey with the first new bottles of Fortuna hitting the market in 2022. In addition to recreating the label and bottles, the bourbon itself aims to be a recreation of the original at its peak in the 1800s. It's made in small (six barrel) batches as a blend of Kentucky straight bourbons aged 6 years. It's bottled at 102 proof and is available for purchase online at Seelbach.com and at KLWines.com as of September 2022.

name: Title No. 21 Rye Whiskey
description: This is a rye whiskey that's named for the amendment to repeal Prohibition. It is matured in new, charred oak barrels. Note: proof varies by bottling, typically 80-90 proof.

name: Belgrove White Rye Whiskey
description: Australian whiskey distillation became legal in the 1990's. Australia's first and only rye whiskey producer, Belgrove Distillery, is owned and operated by farmer Peter Bignell, who utilizes biofuel and sustainability. This White Rye Whiskey is unaged and consists of 100% rye, grown onsite. It is bottled at 40% ABV.

name: Old Overholt Straight Rye Whiskey (80 proof)
description: This brand is named after Abraham Overholt, a Pennsylvania farmer that had switched his focus from farming to distilling in the early 1800s.  At beginning of Prohibition, the whiskey was granted a medicinal license and the popularity of the brand surged.  The Pennsylvania brand has survived, but has been produced in Kentucky for some time now and is currently owned by Beam Suntory.

tastingNotes.full: Next time you take a shot of this rye, take a minute and actually smell the whiskey.  You'll notice a pleasing aroma full of dark grain, char smoke, and cherry vanilla cola.  The whiskey is quite hollow on your palate and not very full, but the finish is pleasing enough.  You are left with the dark grain and char wood aromas.

name: Chattanooga Whiskey 99 Rye
description: Chattanooga Whiskey 99 Rye made from a four-grain mash bill with over 60% of the recipe containing malted rye which is slow-toasted and drum roasted. After a seven day fermentation, it is distilled and aged for at least 3 years in 53-gallon charred oak barrels. Each batch is made from 6-10 barrels. The whiskey is bottled at 99 proof and available beginning July 2020.

tastingNotes.full: With three different types of malted rye, this whiskey stands out in the category. Sweet and gentle for its 99-proof, it brings notes of vanilla, creme brulee, and ripe cherry, and a toasty finish with a touch of baked pear.

name: Cask & Crew Rye Whiskey Blend
caskType: new, charred American oak and new, uncharred American oak
description: A blend of two whiskeys from two countries. The first comprises 51% of the blend; a Canadian rye whiskey aged in new charred American oak barrels. The remainder is a Kentucky corn mash whiskey aged in new un-charred oak. The whiskeys are aged for three years in their respective barrels of which are of the 53-gallon size.

tastingNotes.full: The color is dark for a 3-year old whiskey, especially with 51% Canadian rye. Alcohol-forward nose with a little earth and grains. Palate is rough and bitter, like over-brewed black tea. Some flavors of grains, oak and vanilla and a touch of fruit. Short, slightly hot and bitter finish with a little corn, vanilla and oak.

tastingNotes.palate: Palate is rough and bitter, like over-brewed black tea. Some flavors of grains, oak and vanilla and a touch of fruit. Short, slightly hot and bitter
tastingNotes.finish: finish with a little corn, vanilla and oak

name: Low Gap Clear Rye Whiskey
description: Made using 100% malted rye in a small cognac pot still (16 hectoliter's to be exact), this un-aged rye comes in just shy of 86 proof. Low Gap is a line of whiskeys from the folks at Craft Distillers, a microdistillery based in California.

name: Chattanooga Whiskey Experimental Single Batch Series Batch 009: Tennessee Double Malt
Chattanooga Whiskey Experimental Single Batch Series Batch 010: Tennessee Double Barrel
Chattanooga Whiskey Co. 1816 Reserve
description: The 1816 Reserve is one of two introductory whiskeys from Chattanooga Whiskey Co. which after a "Vote Whiskey" campaign in 2012, became the city's first whiskey brand since Prohibition. This features a mash bill of 75 percent corn, 21 percent rye and 4 percent malted barley, and was sourced from MGP in Indiana. The name “1816” is meant to honor the establishment of the trading post, Ross’s Landing, founded by John Ross, leader of the Cherokee nation and later their Principal Chief. This area later became the town of Chattanooga.

tastingNotes.full: The nose offers a smoky, charred profile, with caramel and molasses. There's also a grainy component, along with rye spice. The mouthfeel is creamy with nutty and buttery flavors and a backbone of spice and vanilla. The finish is short and sharp, with more rye spice, and a touch of cinnamon.

name: Chattanooga Whiskey Co. 1816 Cask
description: The 1816 Cask is the second introductory product from Chattanooga Whiskey Co., the first whiskey brand in Chattanooga since Prohibition. It features the same MGP-sourced whiskey as 1816 Reserve, with a 75 percent corn, 21 percent rye and 4 percent malted barley mash bill. Here though, it's bottled at cask strength, 113.6 proof. Chattanooga Whiskey's Tennessee Stillhouse opened in March 2015, as they begin distilling their own whiskey.

tastingNotes.full: As should be expected, 1816 Cask packs a more potent punch than its 90 proof brother, 1816 Reserve. On the nose, there's caramel and butterscotch, with a rye spiciness and hints of pepper. Lingering in the background are lighter touches of honey, floral and melon. A modest smoky and charred molasses component is discovered as well. Full bodied and smooth, there's a pleasant warming on the finish but no burn, leaving spice as the lasting component. Add a few drops of water to bring out a richer, deeper sweetness, along with baked fruits and honey.

name: Chattanooga Whiskey Barrel Finishing Series: Silver Oak Cabernet Cask Finished
caskType: finished in Silver Oak Cabernet Sauvignon casks
description: This bottling is the third release in the Chattanooga Whiskey's limited edition barrel finishing series. The whiskey is made from a blend of 5 single malt mash bills, each one containing a range of toasted, roasted, and caramel malted barley. The whiskey is aged for over four years including the 18 months in the Silver Oak Cabernet Sauvignon casks. Available in select markets beginning January 2023 and at the brand's Experimental Distillery in downtown Chattanooga. (SRP $59.99)

tastingNotes.full: The aroma initially shows berries and cherry blossoms along with gentle char smoke and a moderate amount of oak. The whiskey is soft on the palate, but picks up speed with an unexpected taste of roasted barley. There's a hearty malt whiskey in the middle that leans a bit herbal. But the wine notes coupled with that help to balance things out. Not sweet or bitter, but fruity and gently smoked. It may not be for everyone, but those looking for something just a bit out of the box will be pleased.

name: Ole Smoky Peanut Butter Whiskey
description: This expression is a sourced whiskey from Tennessee with added peanut butter flavoring. It is bottled with added caramel coloring at 30% ABV.

name: Uncle Nearest 1884 Small Batch Whiskey (Sourced Whiskey)
description: The Uncle Nearest brand honors Nathan "Nearest" Green, a former slave who taught Jack Daniel how to distill. The 1884 Small Batch bottling is named in honor of the year it is believed that Mr. Green last filled barrels of whiskey and retired. Each barrel for the batch is selected by CEO and co-founder Fawn Weaver. In addition, each batch will be curated by a different family descendant of Mr. Green with their name displayed on the back of the bottle. The brand claims a minimum of 7 years for aging although there is no age stated on the bottle. Note: As of 2022, this bottling is being replaced with an 1884 Small Batch Whiskey that is 100% distilled, aged and bottled by Uncle Nearest. The packaging of that whiskey will display a dram of whiskey encased by a horseshoe.

tastingNotes.full: A light, mild and whistle-clean whiskey.  Sugar cookie and sweet grass notes on the nose.  Quite lean on the palate with cinnamon and pastry setting the tone.

name: Ole Smoky Mango Habanero Whiskey
description: This expression is part of the brand's permanent selection of flavored whiskeys. Made in Tennessee, this whiskey is flavored with mango fruit and habanero pepper flavoring. It is bottled at 70 proof.

name: Corsair Mosaic Hopped Whiskey
description: You put beer in my whiskey! No, you put whiskey in my beer! Just drink both! That's the thinking behind this whiskey from Darek Bell at Corsair Distillery, which is a malted barley with Mosaic hops left in the vapor basket as it ferments. Aged for several months.

tastingNotes.full: Of the 4 hopped whiskeys I tasted, this is the most floral of the bunch. The floral and tea-like aromatics definitely tip the see-saw on the beer side away from the malt whiskey side. So much so that except for the evident proof, I'd swear I was tasting a floral, fruity seasonal beer. So if you like floral beers...

name: Jack Daniel's Sinatra Century
description: The love affair between Frank Sinatra and Jack Daniel's is well-known, and on the occasion of what would have been Frank Sinatra's 100th birthday, the whiskey brand decided to pay homage. Jack Daniel's Sinatra Century is a limited release 100-barrel creation, bottled at 100 proof. Master Distiller Jeff Arnett handpicked the barrels to craft a unique expression. Available starting October 2015, each bottle comes enclosed in a gift box, with a selection of previously unreleased Sinatra tunes to listen to while enjoying a dram.

tastingNotes.full: Luscious notes of cocoa sweetness mingle with charcoal smoke and touches of oak, spice, citrus, and tropical fruits - mangoes and pineapples - on the nose. The palate is well-rounded and full, with deep flavors of oak, smoke, and a brown sugar, char-and-molasses-tinged-sweet. Finish is smoky, almost savory, with chocolate, oak and molasses bringing it home. A world apart from the Jack Daniel's you're topping off with Coke.

name: Jim Beam Bonded Bourbon
description: "Bottled in Bond" used to be a code for "the good stuff." Bonded whiskey is subject to regulation and production rules above and beyond those that normally govern the production of whiskey. Aged at least four years, with a higher proof, and in strictly controlled warehouses, this bottle is a return to a classic expression of whiskey.

tastingNotes.full: It's Jim Beam and then some. Honey and spice on the nose, along with oak, cherry, and butterscotch. It's a bold taste, rustic but refined, with vanilla, strong mint, bitter chocolate, and pepper. There's also charcoal, tobacco, and hay. Finish is short but warm, with more wood and mint as well as a bit of caramel. Water tames a bit of the bitterness and accentuates red fruits, chocolate, and pepper.

name: 2bar Bourbon
description: 2 Bar Spirits is a distillery located in Seattle, Washington. The grains used at the distillery are all sourced from the Pacific Northwest. In the case of their bourbon, they use 95% Washington grain and 5% Oregon grain but do not disclose their mash-bill. The whiskey is aged in 15-gallon barrels with a #3 Char level. The bourbons are released in batches, though the bottle reviewed had no such number indicating the batch number.

tastingNotes.full: The aroma of the bourbon seems to lean into the insecticide territory. There are some hay and caramel notes tucked in there, but the medicinal notes take over and are off-putting. Over time, that blows off, but the palate isn't an improvement. The raw grain flavors highlight the young age of the whiskey with too little of a body to sustain you. Cinnamon hots, fresh herbs, and char notes are what you are left with on the finish.

name: FEW Straight Bourbon
description: FEW is a grain-to-glass distillery located in the Chicago suburb of Evanston, Illinois. The grains used in this high-rye bourbon mash bill are sourced from within 100 miles of the distillery. The label for each product depicts an historical image from the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition held in Chicago with the bourbon label depicting the Statue of the Republic, also known as The Golden Lady.

tastingNotes.full: Curry-like spices come to mind on the nose along with a touch of apple juice. The entry is soft and sweet, but turns dry and spicy on the back end. The fruit profile continues with raw peach and apple, but you can taste that youthful quality in the whiskey. All in all, it shows great promise of things to come.

name: Hudson Baby Bourbon (DISCONTINUED)
caskType: small new, charred American oak barrels
description: The first whiskey to be produced by Tuthilltown Spirits, this bourbon is made from 100% New York-grown corn, an unusual mash bill to be sure, but not unheard of. The bourbon is aged in small new, charred American oak (ranging in size from 3-gallons to 14-gallons) for less than four years. The aging is helped along with heavy bass music playing on bass speakers each evening in their warehouse. Typically bottled in 375ml sized bottle, but 750ml are available. Note: This has been discontinued.

tastingNotes.full: In the nose we find CORN...sweet corn, and a tinge of vanilla. The palate is extremely light, with more corn, oak and a bit of sweetened ginger spice. The finish is quick, sweet, and thin.

tastingNotes.palate: The palate is extremely light, with more corn, oak and a bit of sweetened ginger spice
tastingNotes.finish: The finish is quick, sweet, and thin

name: Bardstown Bourbon Co. Château de Laubade Armagnac Finish #2
description: This is the second collaboration between Bardstown Bourbon Co. and Armagnac house Château de Laubade. It features straight bourbons from Kentucky (12 year, mash bill 75% corn, 13% rye, 12% malted barley) and Tennessee (10 year, mash bill 84% corn, 8% rye, 8% malted barley). The bourbon blend is finished in Château de Laubade casks for at least 16 months for some barrels and up to 24 months for others in different warehouse locations. Bottled at 107 proof, there are 2,700 9L cases available as of September 9, 2022 in 20 states, online and at BBCo.'s gift shop in Bardstown.

name: Two Stars Bourbon
description: Two Stars Bourbon is made in Louisville, Kentucky by Clear Spring Distilling Co. (a label owned by Sazerac) and bottled at 86 proof. Although it carries no age statement, as a straight whiskey, it's been aged for at least 2 years.

name: Jefferson's Bourbon Marian McLain (First Release)
description: Jefferson's Bourbon Marian McLain is named after founder Trey Zoeller's 8th generation grandmother, one of the earliest known female bootleggers & whiskey runners in history. The bottling is made from a blend of bourbons as follows: 21% 14 year-old Tennessee straight bourbon; 40% 11 year-old Kentucky straight bourbon; 14% wheated double-barrel bourbon; 17% rum cask finished bourbon; and 8% 8 year-old Kentucky straight bourbon. Bottled at 101 proof, this is available nationwide as of April 2023. (SRP $300)

tastingNotes.full: The nose is classically bourbon-forward, with notes of fresh apples, cherries, baking spices, and a slight nuttiness. The palate, however, is not as heavy as the nose would suggest, with a light to medium richness and subtle notes of bayleaf, oregano, and thyme. The midpalate has flavors akin to honey nut coated breakfast cereal, leading to a fruity finish with a spicy kick.

name: Flatboat Bourbon
description: This 90-proof bourbon is produced by the Sazerac-owned Barton 1792 Distillery in Kentucky. We know from its "straight" labeling that it's been aged for at least 2 years in new, charred American oak. It's a private label brand exclusively for the retail chain, the Liquor Barn.

name: Benchmark No. 8 Bourbon
description: Buffalo Trace is on the registry of National Historic Landmarks, and its long legacy involves a variety of inventive, iconic characters. Many of the whiskeys made at Buffalo Trace are a tribute to their innovative employees, from Col. Blanton to Col. E.H. Taylor to the late Elmer T. Lee, longtime master distiller. Then there are the McAfee brothers, who are known for surveying a site north of Frankfort.

tastingNotes.full: This bourbon may not be the prettiest belle at the ball, but it’s a committed member of the Buffalo Trace Distillery’s bourbon family and it gets the job done.  You can discern some faint flint-like mineral notes behind the peppery spiciness, but other than that, there are no bells or whistles, which is to say: very little complexity. But that might be all that you require when you’re making a simple, easy-drinking cocktail. It delivers floral and honey sweetness on the palate and wraps up with a swift grainy kick. All in a day’s work.

name: 1792 Bottled in Bond Bourbon
description: Available beginning December 2017, this Kentucky straight bourbon from Barton 1792 follows the Bottled in Bond requirements. Among these are: distilled in one season from one distiller, aged at least four years, and bottled at 100 proof.

tastingNotes.full: Apples, pears, baking spice, and leather tickle the nose. The palate takes on an unexpected richness, with toffee adding a base to the fruity and spicy elements. The finish is deep, well rounded, and satisfying. For those looking for a classic bourbon with a bit of heft without going too over-the-top, this is a good one to reach for.

name: Rod & Rifle American Blended Whiskey
description: Rod & Rifle is a line of whiskeys created by Prestige Imports LLC in partnership with Wildlife Forever, the nonprofit conservation extension of the North American Hunting & Fishing Clubs, with hunting and fishing motifs on the bottles. The Blended American Whiskey is sourced from a Tennessee distillery.

tastingNotes.full: This is a rather dry whiskey with lots of tobacco and charcoal texture. Rye bread with a touch of honey and vanilla becomes evident after a couple of sips. Fairly easy to sip with a slight acetone finish. Not bad for its price point, and would be a decent base for cocktails.

name: Hunter's Select Barrel Tennessee Bourbon (Batch 1)
description: Hunter's Select Barrel was created in honor of Colonel Henry Hunter, a veteran of the War of 1812, distillery operator, and the original property owner of the Leiper’s Fork Distillery land. Comprised of 72% corn, 20% rye and 8% malted barley, this sourced whiskey was hand selected and bottled by blending small lots of barrels of finished Tennessee bourbon. It was aged for nine years, five months, and 11 days.

name: Chattanooga Whiskey Founder's 12th Anniversary Blend
description: Formulated each year by CEO & Founder Tim Piersant, Chattanooga Whiskey Founder's 12th Anniversary Blend is made from a blend of three solera whiskeys — each representing the past, present, and future. Representing the past, the brand's high-rye bourbon 1816 makes up 12% of the blend. The present is represented by Barrel 91 which is the brand's signature Tennessee high malt recipe and is 60% of the blend. Meanwhile, the future is featured with their Infinity Barrel with is a blend of malt and rye malt whiskeys including a cherrywood smoked "Danko" rye malt whiskey. Bottled at 100 proof without chill-filtration, it's available in limited quantities beginning May 2024. (SRP $59.99)

tastingNotes.full: The nose shows a mix of sweet, red fruit, and spice along with a touch of vanilla. Further tastes brings out more of the cherrywood smoke. The whiskey is a little chewy with a deep maple flavor. But it's not a sugary sweetness since the oak and barrels spices tame that down a bit. Overall, the flavors are more spice-driven with a touch of herbs on the mid-palate. Meanwhile, the smoke is an underlying element in the whiskey providing some depth and dimension. Finish is bittersweet.

caskType: new, charred American oak w/varying toast levels
description: This bottling marks the sixth release in Chattanooga Whiskey's Bottled in Bond Vintage Series. It was distilled in one season (July 2019-December 2019) at their Riverfront Distillery in Chattanooga, Tennessee from a variety of high-malt bourbon mash bills, each one with at least 25% specialty malted grains. Additionally, a portion of each recipe was aged in custom-toasted and charred barrels designed to compliment it. The Fall 2019 Vintage will be available at the Chattanooga Whiskey Experimental Distillery and across TN, GA, FL, TX, IL, IN, and SC beginning September 2023. (SRP $52.99)

name: Jack Daniel's Tennessee Bicentennial
description: This limited edition expression from Jack Daniel's was released in 1995 to celebrate the bicentennial of Tennessee's statehood. The whiskey is presented in a bottle that is a replica of a bottle designed and made by Jack Daniel himself 100 years earlier to celebrate Tennessee's centennial.

name: Cassius Clay Straight Bourbon Whiskey
description: Cassius Clay Straight Bourbon Whiskey was released in October 2015 by Cary King Bottling Co. in Kentucky. This 100-proof whiskey ages for around 8 years in charred American oak.

name: Heaven's Door Double Barrel Whiskey
caskType: finished in toasted, new American oak
description: Heaven's Door is a whiskey brand developed in collaboration with Bob Dylan. The bottles feature iron gates created by Dylan in his studio, Black Buffalo Ironworks, which were made from found objects from across America including “everything from farm equipment, children’s toys, kitchen utensils and antique firearms to chains, cogs, axes and wheels.” As for the whiskey, it is made from three different whiskeys and finished in toasted, new American oak for an additional year. Bottled at 100 proof.

tastingNotes.full: Chocolate covered raspberries on the nose, with spicy oak, and doughy cinnamon buns topped with glazed brown sugar. Vanilla and dark red fruits on the palate, with plums and berries, alongside par-baked dough, mint, and in the background, flashes of white pepper and licorice. A moderately lengthy finish showcases lasting spice, oak, caramel, peppermint, and cinnamon.

name: Chattanooga Whiskey Cask 111
description: Chattanooga Whiskey Cask 111 is made from a four-grain mash bill which in addition to yellow corn uses three malted grains: rye malt, caramel malted barley, and honey malted barley. Chattanooga refers to this whiskey as a Tennessee High Malt, but technically this is a straight bourbon. Matured for a minimum of two years in toasted and charred barrels, Cask 111 is bottled at barrel strength without filtration at 111 proof.

tastingNotes.full: Chattanooga's Cask 111 retains the balance of Cask 91, but whereas that one is light and easy to drink, this one amps up the proof and flavor. It's spicier than its lower-proof sibling, but the more concentrated spirit also brings out more of the bourbon's depth and sweetness. Vanilla, anise, and leather come through on the palate, with a fruity cherry note lingering on the finish. It's a well-made whiskey and a pleasure to sip at cask strength.

name: Jack Daniel's Tennessee Tasters' Selection Barrel Proof Rye
description: Tennessee Tasters' is a limited edition experimental series and this Barrel Proof Rye is an example of the the brand's Tennessee rye whiskey taken straight from the cask. It is made with a mash bill of 70% rye, 18% corn, and 12% malted barley. The rye whiskey goes through the standard charcoal filtering post-distillation. Available July 2019 at the distillery and at select Tennessee retailers.

name: Rare Character Presents Single Barrel Series Selected By Liquorun,Brazos Bourbon Hounds,BlueBonnet Bourbon Barrel No. AQU-3338 Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey Cask Strength
Brother's Bond Bourbon
description: Brother's Bond Bourbon is a brand founded by American actors Ian Somerhalder and Paul Wesley, co-stars in the TV series "Vampire Diaries" who played the Salvatore Brothers on the show. This is a straight bourbon made from three different mash bills and with four types of grain: corn, rye, wheat, and malted barley. The whiskey aged in virgin, charred oak barrels with the staves getting a #4 char and the heads a #2 char. Available as of May 1, 2021.

tastingNotes.full: The nose begins with cinnamon and cloves, followed by vanilla taffy and ginger. The palate is a bit soft, with doughy wheat bread, milk chocolate, and cedar box followed by peanut brittle, allspice, and black pepper. A short finish offers pecan, peanut brittle, and coffee grounds, with mint and caramel.

name: Yellowstone Select Kentucky Straight Bourbon
description: Created in 1872 by Taylor & WIlliams and named in honor of the national park, the Yellowstone brand has moved around from distillery to distillery since its creation. The current owner, Luxco, sources the bourbon from other distilleries in Kentucky; however, Luxco recently took a 50% stake in the Limestone Branch Distillery, run by Steve and Paul Beam. In February 2015, the Beams put the first batch of their new bourbon in casks, which they plan to release under the Yellowstone label. The Select is a selection of casks chosen by Steve Beam to reflect the heritage of the Yellowstone name, made from four- and seven-year-old, high-rye bourbons.

tastingNotes.full: Light and shy aromas of smoke, dry cider and wood greet the nose. On the palate cider gains confidence, the wood notes get spicier, and suggestions of burnt sugar emerge. The medium finish reprises the wood and gains additional spice.

name: Backbone Bourbon Uncut
description: The name is a tribute to the backbone of America: The Midwest. Each bottle has slight variations to each mash but follows a rough mashbill of 70% corn, 25% rye and finished with malted barley, Backbone is distilled in Lawrenceburg, IN then aged for just under 4 years and bottled "uncut" in Bardstown, KY.. The review is from batch 9 at 116.4 proof.

tastingNotes.full: Fairly dark and rich bronze in color, it smells like dried hay and golden wheat. Fairly full-flavored for the height of proof, with notes of vanilla and grated nutmeg. The body is very pastry-like, similar to the bottom layer of dough that doesn't quite crisp up on the bottom of an apple pie. The alcohol burn stays throughout the finish, muddling some delicate nuances which open up a bit with a few drops of water. Curious to see what a few more years of aging will do to this whiskey.

name: Wilderness Trail 8 Year Bottled in Bond Small Batch Bourbon (Wheated Bourbon)
description: Released in August 2023, this expression is made with the same mash bill as the brand's flagship wheated bourbon — 64% corn, 24% wheat, and 12% malted barley. Wilderness Trail also employs a sweet mash rather than a sour mash in its production. Aged 8 years, this bourbon also adheres to the bottled in bond requirements. (SRP $88)

tastingNotes.full: Really enjoyable nose of vanilla, brown butter, toasted grains and caramel. The taste is a touch hot, but there's a light sweetness and the barrel spices are well integrated on the palate. The body is lean and there are flavors of the grains lean herbal. The finish is of decent length, but could last a bit longer. Adding a splash of water intensifies the herbal notes and softens the body. Drink neat if you don't mind a light heat.

name: Wilderness Trail 6 Year Bottled in Bond Bourbon (Wheated Bourbon)
description: This expression consists of a mash bill of 64% corn, 24% wheat, and 12% barley. It is matured in new, charred, white oak for a minimum of 6 years following Bottled in Bond standards. As such, it is bottled at 100 proof.

name: Forbidden Bourbon
description: This is the first release for the grain-to-glass bourbon brand. Master Distiller Marianne Eaves has partnered with Forbidden's South Carolina-based founders and she crafted this release at Kentucky's Bardstown Bourbon Company where it was distilled, aged, and bottled. For this small batch bourbon, she used white corn, white winter wheat and malted barley and non-traditional low temperature fermentation. It was aged for 5 years and was bottled at 95.2 proof. Available in initially in Kentucky, Tennessee, Georgia, and South Carolina beginning May 2023. (SRP $129)

name: Belle Meade Sour Mash Straight Bourbon
description: Belle Meade is the first release from Nelson's Green Brier after the distillery went silent for Prohibition. Charlie and Andy Nelson discovered the site of their great-great-great grandfather's distillery during a family trip and decided to start up the family business again. The bourbon is made in very small batches, only 4 barrels each, and has a high rye content, based on the original family recipe. The horses on the label are a tribute to the Belle Meade Plantation in Nashville (one of them even had a filly named Bourbon Belle.)

tastingNotes.full: Very balanced and smooth, with caramel corn sweetness, orange, vanilla and just the right touch of leather. The percentage of rye makes for a spicy finish, with lots of allspice, pinecone and black pepper. Bit of an astringent tickle, but not mad at it.

name: Barrell Bourbon Justin's House of Bourbon
Border Bourbon Bottled In Bond Straight Bourbon
Darby's Reserve Rye Whiskey
description: This product is of an unnamed distillery whose new-make has been "purified" by Terressentia Corporation with its TerrePure treatment process. The treatment is designed to accelerate the aging process, allegedly achieving the results of 4 to 6 years of traditional maturation in days. Terressentia offers large liquor stores "turnkey" bottlings by the pallet, sourcing spirits from around the globe, treating them, and designing custom labels for the retailer. Darby's Reserve Rye Whiskey, a "small batch," is  a purified rye whiskey produced for Total Wine & More. By law, American whiskies must pass through new, charred oak for an unspecified period of time; however, Terressentia's website offers no details on barreling. Bottled at 45% ABV.

name: 291 M Colorado Rye Whiskey
caskType: finished with Aspen wood staves & maple syrup barrels

name: Henry DuYore's Rye Whiskey
description: Released in January 2016, this rye whiskey expression is produced by Ransom Spirits in Sheridan, Oregon. This whiskey begins with a mash of 77.8% rye and 22.7% barley. Part of the mash is  distilled in a pot still, with the rest distilled in a column still. After blending, the whiskey is aged 18 months in new, charred American oak.

name: Heaven's Door Straight Bourbon Whiskey
description: Heaven's Door is a whiskey brand developed in collaboration with Bob Dylan. This straight bourbon whiskey is distilled and aged in Tennessee for at least 6 years in new, charred American oak barrels. It's bottled without chill filtration at 92 proof.

name: Chattanooga Whiskey 91
caskType: Toasted and charred oak; finished in charred oak solera
description: Chattanooga Whiskey 91 is made from a four-grain mash bill which in addition to yellow corn uses three malted grains: rye malt, caramel malted barley, and honey malted barley. The mash bill recipe was chosen by master distiller Grant McCracken -- Barrel 91-- from the 100 barrels distilled at the brand's experimental distillery. Chattanooga refers to this whiskey as a Tennessee High Malt, but technically this is a straight bourbon. Matured for a minimum of two years in toasted and charred barrels and is finished in a charred 4000-gallon oak solera barrel.

tastingNotes.full: This new whiskey from Chattanooga is distinguished both by its high-malt mash bill and finishing in a large solera. Everything about it is well-balanced: It's light-bodied but pleasantly strong, with notes of vanilla and only moderate smoky char. A bit of brown sugar sweetness comes through on the palate and the finish is bright with a hint of cedar. Though it doesn't stray too far from a classic bourbon profile, Chattanooga has produced a whiskey that is unique, good, and affordable; that's a promising feat for a new distillery.

name: Ole Smoky Salty Caramel Whiskey
description: This is one of the core expressions from Ole Smoky in Gatlinburg, TN. It is a whiskey of unknown corn-dominant mash bill that has been flavored with unspecified ingredients and colors that contribute toward an intended salted caramel flavor profile. It is bottled at 60 proof.

name: Davidson Reserve Barrel Strength Four Grain Tennessee Straight Bourbon
Corsair Quinoa Whiskey
description: Based in Tennessee, Corsair is a distillery known for its renegade approach to making whiskey. One of Darek Bell's many experimental whiskeys is this one, which is made from both malted barley and red and white quinoa seeds (80% and 20% respectively.)

tastingNotes.full: Dare you to taste it without exclaiming the word "interesting" aloud. Very grassy with a thick, weighty, almost chalky texture that coats the palate. Nutty (cashews, almonds , walnuts) with pretty cinnamon and nutmeg spices and honeysuckle. The sweet and spicy notes are tempered with apricot and dry toasted barley. Very complex. Leaves the sipper guessing, possibly wanting more to figure out what's happening.

name: Chattanooga Whiskey Bottled in Bond (Fall 2018 Vintage)
description: This Fall 2018 Bottled in Bond release from Chattanooga Whiskey is the fourth such release for the distillery. It is comprised of 4 high malt bourbons that each contain 25% specialty malted grains in their mash bills, all distilled in the fall of 2018 (July-December). The specialty malts used here include cherrywood smoke malt, naked oak malt and de-husked chocolate malt. As per bottled-in-bond requirements, it is bottled at 100 proof. Availability begins in September 2022 in select US markets. (SRP $52.99)

name: Corsair Centennial Hopped Whiskey
description: Corsair Master Distiller is always searching for new ways to experiment with whiskey and push its boundaries. This is where close cousins beer and whiskey finally meet. While fermenting traditional malted barley, he keeps Centennial hops in the vapor basket to impart flavor.

tastingNotes.full: Unlike the Galaxy, this one smells less immediately like beer. It's also much more malty and fruitier (melon and peaches) on the palate. Ginger, grapefruit peel and spicy clove edge their way in to bring it into the finish. The hop flavors definitely create an unusual  bitter characteristic, but it's not without its malty charms.

name: Jack Daniel's Bonded Rye
description: Launched in September 2023, this is the third release in the brand's Bonded Series and the first bottled in bond rye whiskey released in its history. Like the other rye whiskeys in its portfolio, this is made with a mash bill recipe of 70% rye, 18% corn, and 12% malted barley. It was charcoal mellowed prior to aging in new toasted & charred American oak barrels. It was made in one distilling season (the first batch was distilled in spring 2016) and was aged for a minimum of 4 years in a government bonded warehouse. It is bottled at 100 proof (50% ABV). This is a permanent addition to the brand's portfolio. (SRP $31.99/700ml)

tastingNotes.full: The aroma is full of dried fruits (apple, cherry) along with a hearty rye grain flavor, maple syrup, and a light char. The body of the rye is medium-light on the palate and while there's a light sweetness on the taste, it finishes with a tangy cherry flavor with a mix of barrel spices. Finish is average, but the price is right. The proof makes it a great mixer.

name: Jack Daniel's Master Distiller Series No. 3
description: Created to honor each of the seven Master Distillers at Jack Daniel's, the third in the series is dedicated to Lemuel “Lem” Tolley. He was the grandnephew of Jack himself and held the position from 1941 and 1964, overseeing production during Brown-Forman's purchase of the Tennessee distillery in 1956. From what we gather, he was a "stern" fella determined to increase the distillery's whiskey production without compromising on quality.

name: Corsair Citra Double IPA Hopped Whiskey
description: Corsair Master Distiller Darek Bell is always looking to push the envelope and take risks when it comes to whiskey making. This is the fine line where beer and whiskey meet in the same bottle (as opposed to side by side in a bar.) It's fermented with traditional malted barley that has Citra Double IPA hops in the vapor basket to impart their flavor.

tastingNotes.full: The nose is spicy and citrusy. On the palate it's a mix of malted cocoa, grapefruit (both peel and pulp), tangerine (same), lemon (you get the picture), lemongrass, ginger and clove. Like the other hopped whiskeys in the range, it's more bitter than sweet, like beer, though somehow still manages to have enough of a malty kick. For fans of spicy whiskeys who also like beer, this would be something fun to sip.

name: Backroom Bourbon
description: Backroom Bourbon is a blend of sourced straight bourbons between 5 and 10 years old bottled in Washington, D.C. It has a mash bill: of 75% corn, 21% unmalted rye and 4% barley.

name: Bulleit Bourbon Barrel Strength
description: Released in April 2016, Bulleit Bourbon Barrel Strength is made from the same high-rye mash bill as the original expression. The barrels selected were combined into a single batch for bottling at Stitzel-Weller in Louisville, Kentucky. As the name implies, this version is uncut and unfiltered straight from the barrel. Each batch will vary in ABV, ranging between 118 and 125 proof.

tastingNotes.full: Starting with a warm toasted-marshmallow and oak scent, this creamy whiskey's heat comes with lots of pepper. The taste isn't any different: peppery and delightful, hot, and full of dark stone fruit. Fennel and anise hang out on the back end with a pleasant acidity. This is a whiskey to sip and enjoy as it develops.

name: Jeppson's Straight Bourbon
description: This expression is a blend of straight bourbons made from a mash bill of 75% corn, 21% rye, and 4% barley from barrels sourced from Indiana, Kentucky, and Tennessee. These are each aged a minimum 4 years and bottled non chill-filtered at 100 proof.

name: Bighorn Bourbon
description: Bighorn Bourbon Whiskey from Willie's Distillery in Ennis, Montana is a blend of bourbons of varying ages. It is named for the Rocky Mountain Bighorn Ram which like the whiskey, is comfortable on the rocks.

name: Wild Turkey Kentucky Straight Bourbon
description: Aged a minimum of 5 years in new American oak barrels with an "alligator char" (char no. 4). Formerly known as Wild Turkey 81, a package redesign and straightforward name change to Wild Turkey Kentucky Straight Bourbon occurred in 2016.

tastingNotes.full: On the nose, you'll find vanilla, peaches, corn, and rye. The palate is full of oak and shows the woody influences of charred sugars, nutmeg, and other baking spices. There's a minty hint found throughout the bourbon and the finish is moderate in length with sweet corn, apples, and dark rye.

name: New Riff 4 Year Single Barrel Bourbon
description: New Riff Single Barrel Bourbon is made with the same mash bill as the brand's standard bourbon release: 65% corn, 30% rye, and 5% malted barley. These single barrel releases are selected by retailers or on-premise locations. Each single barrel bottling is aged for at least 4 years in 53-gallon new, charred American oak barrels. Additionally, they are bottled at barrel proof without chill-filtration so expect to see variances in both flavor and proof with each barrel.

tastingNotes.full: New Riff Single Barrel Barrel Proof Bourbon combines a classic bourbon profile with the brashness of a moderately aged whiskey bottled at barrel proof. It has a light mouthfeel, but is bursting with spice and notes of vanilla, white pepper, and candied orange peel. It's a very solid value, especially given its high proof. The whiskey has ample character to stand up in cocktails and is also quite enjoyable neat.

name: Low Gap 2 Year Rye Whiskey
caskType: New American Oak + Used Bourbon & Cognac Barrels
description: Made with 100% malted rye, this two year rye has spent time in new American Oak barrels as well as used bourbon and cognac barrels. The Low Gap whiskeys are double distilled on an antique 16HL cognac still and are produced by Craft Distillers located in Mendocino County, CA.

name: Copper Fox Original Rye Whiskey
caskType: ex-bourbon + new & used apple wood and oak chips
description: Copper Fox Original Rye Whiskey centers around using new and used apple wood and oak chips to flavor the house-made malt during drying as well as when the whiskey is aging in the used bourbon barrels. The mash bill itself is 2/3rd parts rye and 1/3rd malted barley with all grains sourced from Virginia.

tastingNotes.full: This young firecracker of a rye starts out with a note of raw sawdust, indicating relatively short aging time, and apple smoke. The youth makes itself even more apparent in the palate, with raw wood and hot alcoholic notes. Instead of apple, the cherry makes itself known on the mid-palate, along with the malty sweetness. The biscuity malt fades to the back on the finish, but leaves a bit of an unpleasant bitterness at the very end. Copper Fox Original Rye Whiskey has good bones to it, but needs more time in the barrel.

name: Nelson Brothers Rye Whiskey
description: This Rye Whiskey is the third product in the Nelson Brothers portfolio and the first rye from Nelson's Green Briar Distillery since before Prohibition. Since the original pre-Prohibition recipe was lost, co-founder & Head Distiller Andy Nelson and his team decided to invert the corn and rye used in the brand's bourbon recipe for this release. Announced in October 2023, availability is expected in markets nationwide. (SRP $36.99)

tastingNotes.full: Vanilla and spearmint lead on the nose, along with cloves, cinnamon, and sour cherries. The palate starts dry, with cedar, rye spice, and barrel char, and also offers expressed orange peel, brown sugar, burnt toasted, and spent coffee grounds. The finish turns richer, with chocolate syrup, caramel, and corn bread, as well as black pepper. A balanced rye that bourbon drinkers would appreciate as opposed to the 95% ryes so prevalent on the market.

name: Great Northern Rye Whiskey
description: Great Northern Rye Whiskey is distilled in Wisconsin and made from a mashbill of locally grown raw rye grain, rye malt, and corn, all sourced within 150 miles of the distillery. It's bottled at 48% ABV after aging in new, charred American oak.

name: Silver Release Bourbon Whiskey
description: This bourbon is made by Knox Whiskey Works in Knoxville, Tennessee. It's made from locally sourced heirloom corn and aged in new, charred American oak. It is bottled at 45% ABV.
